title: "Spatial Audio Perception in Interactive Virtual Reality: Quality Evaluation

description: >
  Quality evaluation of spatial audio in interactive VR, combining behavioural
  and cognitive measures with conventional perceptual ratings.

Conventional audio quality evaluation asks listeners to rate what they hear.
In interactive virtual reality that is only part of the picture: participants
move through the scene, and where they go, what they look at, and how hard they
are working are all evidence about what they perceive.

This thesis develops and validates evaluation methods for spatial audio in
interactive virtual environments, treating exploration behaviour and cognitive
load as measurements in their own right rather than as noise to be controlled
away. It spans direct and indirect evaluation methods, the influence of visual
content and scene complexity on audio quality judgments, and the methodological
framework needed to make such experiments reproducible.

Supervised at the **International Audio Laboratories Erlangen**, a joint
institution of Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg and Fraunhofer IIS.
